# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Monthly Report (April 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In April 2026, development focused on hardening the Superchain infrastructure through critical updates to the Kona client and a comprehensive sweep of bug fixes across core components. A significant milestone was reached in the interoperability roadmap, with the successful verification of `kona-interop` within the `op-challenger` environment. Efforts also centered on refining the accuracy of the protocol's error handling and data validation, ensuring that the registry and its associated services maintain high standards of reliability as the ecosystem scales.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Kona Client & Prestate Management
The registry continues to serve as the source of truth for valid network states. A primary focus this month was the integration of updated prestates to support the evolving Kona client.
*   **Kona 1.2.12 Integration:** Added new standard prestates for Kona version 1.2.12 to the registry, specifically updating `validation/standard/standard-prestates.toml` [#1206](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1206).

### Interoperability & Dispute Logic
Significant progress was made in the testing and documentation of cross-chain interoperability features.
*   **Challenger Host Refinement:** Resolved issues with host arguments in the Kona super executor. The `op-challenger` runner is now successfully executing `kona-interop` in test environments, marking a key step forward for the Superchain's fault proof system [#18287](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18287).
*   **Transaction Pool Behavior:** Formalized the documentation for interoperability transaction pool eviction. It was confirmed that `op-reth` will drop all interop executing messages upon any reorg to ensure implementation simplicity and maximum safety [#19351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19351).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Dispute Game Migration:** The transition of FaultDisputeGame chains to the SuperDisputeGame model saw administrative progress, with redundant issues being consolidated to streamline the migration path [#19013](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19013).
*   **Protocol Documentation:** Closed out tasks related to documenting reorg behaviors and fixing executor arguments for the challenger service.

### New & Active Issues
A high volume of technical debt and bug reports were identified across the OP Stack:
*   **Core Logic Errors:** Issues were raised for `op-batcher` regarding incorrect L1 origin comparisons [#19859](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19859) and `op-node` regarding channel size calculation errors during frame pruning [#19858](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19858).
*   **Type Handling & Messaging:** Several bugs were identified in `op-service` where `UnmarshalText` functions for `Bytes256` and `Blob` were reporting incorrect type names (e.g., labeling them as `Bytes32`), which could lead to developer confusion [#19862](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19862), [#19864](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19864).
*   **Resource Management:** A leak in `CachingReceiptsProvider` was identified where fetching locks are not properly released on errors, potentially impacting service stability [#19875](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19875).
*   **Contract Clarity:** Discrepancies between `require` statements and their corresponding error messages were found in `LivenessModule` and `SystemConfig`, highlighting a need for better consistency in the `contracts-bedrock` codebase [#19866](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19866), [#19868](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19868).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month was characterized by active technical coordination between maintainers. Notable discussions involved **karlfloersch** and **stevennevins** regarding the strategic alignment of the transaction pool's reorg behavior and the consolidation of the SuperDisputeGame migration strategy. The resolution of the `op-challenger` host arguments by **ajsutton** demonstrates effective cross-component collaboration, ensuring that the Kona executor integrates seamlessly with the broader Optimism infrastructure. The community's focus remains on high-precision fixes to the OP Stack's foundational services.
